Per discussions with Jack Humphrey, adding the requirement of ‘may be repeated a third time only in exceptional circumstances and onlywith authorization of thedeanof the college in which the student is enrolled.'to s8.33.31 would require students to get approval from the dean of their college.

BS - Biotechnology, effective Fall 2026 Appendix D Biotechnology education relies heavily on inquiry-based, experiential learning.
The Biotechnology program at the University of Rhode Island provides students with lecture- and laboratory-based opportunities to engage in active learning, apply scientific concepts, and develop analytical, critical- thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Students additionally gain real-world experience through experiential learning projects, undergraduate research, and internships that prepare them for employment in biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries as well as academic and clinical research settings.
Beginning in Fall 2026, the Biotechnology program will implement a program fee to ensure that students continue to receive high-quality, modern laboratory experiences.
Current introductory laboratory courses (BTC 111 and BTC 195) require costly consumables and instrumentation that cannot be adequately supported by the existing course-specific fees.
The program fee will allow for modernization of curriculum and laboratory offerings, the purchase and maintenance of updated equipment, and the development of new laboratory exercises.

These changes support a sustainable, high-impact educational experience without increasing individual per-course financial burdens.
